text:
Huge stones, red sun and dust

raised in clouds over dry earth...

The sun, as it left, murmured in my ear:

you have your soul never dead.


Moving serpents at my side

raised their heads to my mouth.

The gray sky, the stone, repeated:

you have your soul never dead.


Vulture beaks were felt later

beside my feet stirring the earth;

voices of the plain the afternoon repeated:

you have your soul never dead.


Oh fertile sun, enflamed earth,

starry sky, enormous sea, forest,

enter my soul, shake it.

This poor one sleeps who seems dead.


Ah, may your eyes awaken, soul,

and find the world as something new...

Ah, may your eyes awaken, soul,

soul that sleeps with a dead smell...

translation.title: Dead Soul
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps the strange repeated assurance that the soul is never dead.
